title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
blurb: Cal Newport, a computer science professor, argues that the ability to concentrate without distraction on demanding tasks is becoming rarer just as it becomes more valuable. He calls this deep work, and contrasts it with shallow work: emails, meetings, and logistics that anyone could do while distracted. In the first half, he makes the case that deep work helps you learn hard things quickly and produce excellent results. He shows how modern workplaces quietly undermine it by treating busyness as a sign of productivity. He also argues that a focused life is a more meaningful one. In the second half, he offers four rules: build routines that protect deep work, train yourself to tolerate boredom, be choosy about social media and other tools, and ruthlessly limit shallow tasks.

lessons.t: Deep Work Is Rare and Valuable
lessons.b: The ability to focus intensely is becoming more valuable just as it becomes rarer, which makes it a professional superpower.
Without clear ways to measure output, workplaces default to visible busyness like fast email replies, which crowds out deep work.
Deep work sticks when you pick a scheduling style that fits your life and support it with rituals for where, when, and how you work.
